Our Vision
At Central Park Primary School the whole school community is involved in raising the achievement and attainment of all children. We aim to instil a life-long love of learning within a secure and stimulating environment, and through our innovative teaching we will provide the children with a personalised, challenging curriculum. We believe that every child really does matter and that we have a duty to empower each child to become a successful, responsible citizen of the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Central Park Primary School - After School Club
pageCache.text:
AFTER SCHOOL CLUBS
Joining a club means you get to step outside of your everyday routine, dive into new experiences and learn new skills. You'll meet people who share your interests and work together on exciting projects. And, let's not forget the feeling of accomplishment when you see your hard work pay off, whether it's a finished art piece, a winning debate, or a game you programmed from scratch!
But it's not just about the end result - it's about the journey. After-school clubs are a space where you can express yourself freely, without fear of judgement. You can try new things, make mistakes, and learn from them. You'll discover strengths you never knew you had and build confidence in yourself.
So, say goodbye to boring afternoons and hello to a world of excitement and possibility. Join an after-school club and discover a whole new side of yourself and your school!
MONDAY - FRIDAY: 3:15 PM TO 4:30 PM
WHERE DO I PICK MY CHILD UP FROM?
FROM THE KEY STAGE 2 PLAYGROUND ENTRANCE ON THACKERAY ROAD
RESERVATIONS AND PAYMENT
THROUGH THE "TEACHERS2PARENTS" APP
WHAT SNACK DO I GIVE MY CHILD?
Give your child a healthy packed lunch for them to eat after school. This could be a sandwich, fruit, pasta, or even a traditional homemade dish. Avoid processed foods that are high in sugar and salt like chocolates, gummy bears, candy, or highly salted crisps.
I AM STRUGGLING FINANCIALLY,
CAN I GET SOME HELP?
Book an appointment with Rachel Egbulonu on: 0770 252 0935 or by email rachel.egbulonu@centralpark.newham.sch.uk
We will try our best to help you in all the ways we can.
TESTIMONIALS FROM CHILDREN
“I absolutely love it!” – Year 5 Pupil
“I really like the clubs because it makes you practice the things you can't do at home and it encourages you.” – Year 3 Pupil
“I feel happy in the clubs.” – Year 2 Pupil
“All the PE teachers are amazing and nice. They are really funny. They are good teachers.” - Year 4 Pupil
TO SIGN UP FOR CLUBS:
DOWNLOAD THE 'TEACHERS2PARENTS' APP ON YOUR PHONE
ENTER YOUR MOBILE PHONE NUMBER
CODE GETS SENT TO YOUR PHONE NUMBER, ENTER THIS CODE INTO THE APP
CLICK ON THE HAMBURGER MENU ON THE TOP LEFT
SELECT THE CLUBS YOU WANT TO BOOK BY CLICKING ON THE PLUS SIGN NEXT TO THE CLUBS
ONCE YOU HAVE CHOSEN ONE OR MORE CLUBS, CLICK ON THE BASKET IN THE TOP RIGHT CORNER
CLICK ON PAY AND ENTER YOUR CARD DETAILS

pageCache.pageTitle: Central Park Primary School - RSHE Consultation
pageCache.text:
RSHE Parent Consultation
Dear Families
We are now in our final stage of consultation for the RSHE policy September 2026. As we have explained over our consultation process there is very limited change for us, when compared to the 2019 version. We have confidence in our RSHE delivery and we already meet much of the changes that are being requested.
By now there has been a wide range of consultation options across the federation and you will see attached the action plan that demonstrates this consultation process since the start of the year. We thank you for your views and support. We are now in a position to share our draft policy. This was created in partnership with Newham PSHE association, that works alongside Newham Sacre and all Newham stakeholders, to create a policy that is supportive to Newham pupils and families.
This draft policy has been taken to our committee governor group and we will now take it, as a final stage to our Full Governing Board, 01st July for ratification and publication on our website ready for September 2026.
Whilst this is a statutory guidance and policy by government, you will note that we have the opportunity to personalise it to meet the needs of our own pupils and families. We feel we have written a policy to meet our federation needs.
Whilst this is in the last stages of completion we still welcome thoughts and questions. If you do have any thoughts and questions they must be taken to the front office, at each school, in the federation and I will return contact. For any views and questions to be considered they must be shared by Wednesday 17th June.
On the request from families, we have translated the policy into Urdu, Bengali and Arabic (THIS HAS BEEN GENERATED BY AN ONLINE PLATFORM SO PLEASE DO NOTE THERE MAY BE SOME INACCURACIES) These can be found above. If you would like the policy translated into another language, please let the school office know with your name and contact details.
This consultation has no links to the unit of work being taught next week 'This is Me' - 'Changing and Growing' - 'Changing Adolescent Bodies' w/b 15th June. Next week follows the previous policy 2019 and remains statutory. Please note that the only non statutory content being taught next week is 'How babies are made' in year 6. If you do not wish your child to take part in that lesson you must ensure that you let the school know.
Federation Head of Education

Finding out more about our Curriculum
If you would like to find out more about the curriculum at Central Park Primary School, we encourage you to speak with your child’s class teacher in the first instance, as they can provide detailed information about what is being taught and how learning is supported in class. For an overview of our curriculum approach, subject areas, and how we ensure progression across year groups. If you would like further information about a specific subject or the overall curriculum design, please contact a member of the Senior Leadership Team, who will be happy to discuss our curriculum intent, implementation, and impact in more detail.
EYFS - Nursery & Reception
For more information on the EYFS curriculum please speak with Mrs Atiyya Musa, Assistant Headteacher.
KS1 - Year 1 & Year 2
For more information on the KS1 curriculum please speak with Ms Julia Scott, Assistant Headteacher.
LKS2 - Year 3 & Year 4
For more information on the LKS2 curriculum pleasee speak with Mr Paul Strange, Assistant Headteacher.
UKS2 - Year 5 & Year 6
For more information on the UKS2 curriculum please speak with Miss Aabida Patel, Assistant Headteacher.
How to contact us
Email: info@centralpark.newham.sch.uk
Telephone: 020 8472 5588
In person: All our senior leaders are on the school gates at the start and end of each day.

Nursery
At Central Park Primary School we aim to provide a happy, caring and stimulating learning environment where all children are encouraged to make progress from their individual starting points. Every child is at the heart of our curriculum, which has been built to ensure that no child is left behind. We believe that children learn best through hands on experiences that are provided both indoors and outdoors. Children will develop positive attitudes towards learning as they are provided with a curriculum that meets their developmental needs. We allow the children to make choices about the activities they want to participate in. Time is given each day to the direct teaching of reading, phonics and mathematics. This ensures that our children are challenged and prepared for the Year 1 Curriculum and beyond.
Our curriculum is underpinned on the four guiding principles of EYFS which help to shape the Early Years Foundation Stage Policy.

pageCache.pageTitle: Central Park Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
We are delighted that you have chosen to visit the online home of Central Park Primary School. Our school is committed to providing high-quality learning opportunities for every child within a safe, secure, and stimulating environment.
At Central Park Primary School, we deliver inspiring teaching that sparks curiosity and nurtures a lifelong love of learning. We are dedicated to providing pupils with the tools and skills they need to grow, thrive, and succeed, both academically and personally. Supporting curious minds and kind hearts lies at the centre of everything we do, alongside a strong focus on pupils being happy and healthy. We work hard to ensure every child feels seen, valued, and supported, and we actively support pupils and families as they navigate challenges together.
With high expectations for all, we encourage our pupils to aim high and become confident, resilient learners and critical thinkers, who will be ready to navigate the challenges of an ever-evolving world. Our learning experiences are carefully designed to provide meaningful opportunities that open doors for children, helping them to discover their strengths, broaden their horizons, and reach their full potential. Education is not just about academic standards but about finding something that sparks a passion within a child, something they want to do, something they enjoy whether it be music, painting, looking at maps or, as in my case, a lifelong passion for history.
Our school motto, Learning Now for Future Success, reflects our commitment to preparing pupils for life in modern Britain and beyond. We strive to equip every child with the skills, confidence, and sense of responsibility they need to flourish, growing into thoughtful, respectful, and capable citizens of the future. Guided by our core values of Honesty, Kindness, and Respect, these principles shine through in the way our children learn, play, and grow together each day.
We are proud of our dedicated and enthusiastic team of staff and governors, who work tirelessly to ensure Central Park Primary School continues to thrive. Above all, we are immensely proud of our wonderful children—their achievements, creativity, and enthusiasm for learning.
This website offers a glimpse into life at Central Park Primary School; however, the best way to truly appreciate what makes our school such a special place is to visit us and see it in action.
We look forward to welcoming you to our school community.
Central Park Primary School | Hosted by New Era Technology

French Vision
Our aim is to support children to communicate in French with confidence, and to teach language that is useful in everyday situations. Learning French increases and deepens understanding of how language works and allows children to explore the similarities and differences between French, English and the other languages that they speak. We recognise language learning as an opportunity for cross-curricular exploration and social development.
Through learning another language children learn to value all the languages spoken by our school community and become curious about the world around them and the various cultures in it. Every lesson reinforces this guiding principle: language brings people together.
What a French lesson looks like:
Grammar points explicitly taught
Phonics explicitly taught
Opportunities for reading, speaking, listening and writing in French
A spiral curriculum which embeds core vocabulary and language skills
Key skills practised in a group and through individual work
Use of appropriate digital and hard copy reference materials

Parent Governor Elections 2026
Governing Body for CPD Schools Federation
Election for Two Parent Governors
Following the resignation of Ms Vic Sorel-Cameron and Ms Rebecca Falzon, Parent Governors, one vacancy exist on the Governing Board for a Parent Governor. If you wish to seek nomination as an elected Parent Governor, please collect a nomination form from the School Office. This form should be completed, with the accompanying personal statement of no more than 150 words, and returned to the Clerk of the Board, Mrs Alix Williams who can be reached at all three of the Federation Schools, no later than 3.30 p.m. on Wednesday 07th October 2026.
GOVERNORS
Central Park Primary School is a caring community in which the staff, pupils, governors and parents are mindful of their responsibilities towards one another. We hope that education in Central Park Primary School will be beneficial, stimulating, well-structured and, above all, an enjoyable experience.
The Governing Board
On the 1st June 2018, the CPD Federation was formally established and our new governing body came into effect. The governing body is made up of elected staff and parent governors, a local authority governor and co-opted governors. Our governing body will meet formally each half term, with attendance information being updated on this page regularly. The governors will also come into both schools at various points in the year to work with various staff members, the children and parents.
What do our Governors do?
The CPD Federation Governing Boards purpose is to provide confident, strategic leadership and to create robust accountability, oversight and assurance for educational and finacial performance.
The 3 core functions of the Governing Board are: - Ensure clarity of vision, ethos and strategic direction - Holding Executive Leaders ro account for the educational performance of the school and its pupils, and the performance management of staff. - Overseeing the finacnail performance of the school and making sure its money is well spent.
To view the finacial benchmarking for Central Park Primary, please click on the link below:
https://schools-financial-benchmarking.service.gov.uk/school?urn=130995
How can I speak to a Governor? If you want to raise a concern with a parent governor please speak to Paul Taylor (Headteacher). If we cannot help you we will refer your concern to a parent governor to contact you. If you would like to go straight to a parent governor then please go to the school office and leave your contact details, or a written query, and it will be passed onto a parent governor.
In accordance with the latest statutory guidance, please click on each governor's image to read further information about them.
Local Advisory Forum (LAF) - What is the LAF?
The LAF is a dedicated group of individuals who come together to support the Governance of the Federation. They provide the local tier of Governance in each school following the scheme of delegation. Their role is to:
- Provide input and perspectives on the direction of the school.
- Collaborate on decision related to school improvement.
- Act as a bridge between the school and our community.
- Review and discuss the progress made against the school plan and self evaluation.
- Review and discuss policies focussed around the school.

Admissions
This section covers Admissions to Central Park Primary School (Reception to Year 6) and Primary to Secondary Transitions. Fair Access The law requires that each local authority must have a Fair Access Protocol (FAP), agreed with the majority of schools in its area to ensure that for In Year admissions unplaced children, especially the most vulnerable, are offered a place at a suitable school as quickly as possible. In agreeing a protocol, the local authority must ensure that no school - including those with available places - is asked to take a disproportionate number of children who have been excluded from other schools, or who have challenging behaviour. Central Park Primary has signed up to the LB Newham’s Fair Access Protocol. https://www.newham.gov.uk/schools-education/fair-access-protocol-secondary-schools-newham Children can be placed on the waiting list for the nursery after the age of 2 years. We will then let you know by letter when we have a place for your child—usually around the time they are 3½ years old. At that point, you will be given a date when you can meet the Early Years Leaders and register your child, and another date for your child to start in the nursery. Children join our reception class in September as we currently have a single point of entry. We arrange meetings for parents in the term before their child goes into a reception class.
Reception Admission for September 2026 entry
RECEPTION ADMISSIONS - A summary of the key steps you need to take to apply for a place in Reception for children born from 1 September 2020 to 31 August 2021.
The national closing date for on time reception applications is 15th January 2026. All reception 2026 applications must be made through the family’s home local authority.
For children living in Newham families must apply via London Borough of Newham. For children living outside Newham, whose family wants them to attend this school their application must be made through their home borough naming this school as a preference on their application.
Remember, parents/carers must apply for a reception place in this school, even if the child has a brother or sister attending this school.
Before submitting a reception application we strongly recommend all families read the autumn 2026 edition of the local authorities ‘Starting School in Newham' guide and find out information about the school you are interested in.
In Year admissions into primary school (aka mid term and mid phase)
IN YEAR ADMISSIONS - If you want to apply for a primary or secondary school place in Newham once the school year has started a family must complete and submit an in-year school admission application. If a family arrives in Newham during the school year and their child needs a school place they must complete an In Year form naming their preferred schools. https://www.newham.gov.uk/schools-education/year-admissions/1 School places are usually offered within 10 days.
The place offered may not be at the school the family prefers as that school may not have a suitable place available.
We recommend you use the Newham School Finder tool to determine the location of your preferred Newham schools and calculate home to school distances.
Secondary Transition
SECONDARY SCHOOL ADMISSIONS - For our children in year 6 this academic year, Starting Secondary School is the composite prospectus for all secondary school admissions in Newham.

Attendance, Absence and Punctuality
Your child is expected to attend school every day unless they are ill or have a medical appointment. If your child is absent from school, please let us know the reason by either phoning the school, writing a note or telling your child’s teacher. If you do not let us know, you may be visited by our Education Welfare Officer. We may also ask her to visit you if you give unsatisfactory reasons for absence, if your child is absent a great deal, or if your child is persistently late.
Our Attendance Journey
Holidays during the school term
You will be required to obtain permission from the headteacher if you want to take your child out of school during term time.
You can only do this if you make an application to the headteacher in advance and there are exceptional circumstances for the holiday. The headteacher will make the decision in how many days your child can be away from school if leave is granted.
You can be fined for taking your child on holiday during term time without the school's permission.
